lines.text: Base branch sets the bough a new worktree grows from. And Create from always gets a new worktree.

lines.speaker: Oak
lines.text: The app remembers your last choice. You picked Current checkout on Anchorage, so switch back to New worktree.

lines.speaker: Oak
lines.text: When in doubt, a new worktree. It keeps main clean, and it still runs on your machine.

lines.speaker: Oak
lines.text: Done somewhere else, and your own deck stayed untouched. That's Cloud.

lines.speaker: Oak
lines.text: Fen's got crews that won't stop tangling. His boardwalk's just behind me.

lines.speaker: Oak
lines.text: Ring the gondola bell if you like, Captain. She's always running.

lines.speaker: Fen
lines.text: Oak sends the crews my way, Captain. See him first.

lines.speaker: Fen
lines.text: Ah, a captain! We used to run every crew down the Great Hall trough. Watch this.

lines.speaker: Fen
lines.text: Three tasks, one folder. Their work blurs together.

lines.speaker: Fen
lines.text: So now each crew gets its own channel. Turn the tiles, then open the gates.

lines.speaker: Fen
lines.text: The Gate Board's right here, Captain. Give every crew its own channel.

lines.speaker: Fen
lines.text: Two crews in one race! Their changes blur together, like two tasks in one folder. Give each its own channel.

lines.speaker: Fen
lines.text: That ran into the Great Hall: your main checkout. A new worktree keeps a session's changes out of main.

lines.speaker: Fen
lines.text: That water turned another crew's wheel. A session's diff should stay with that session.

lines.speaker: Fen
lines.text: It stops short. Follow it down from the gate.

lines.speaker: Fen
lines.text: One crew, one channel. Lovely! Now the other two want their water.

lines.speaker: Fen
lines.text: Three crews, three channels, one spring. That's one repository with a worktree for each session.

lines.speaker: Fen
lines.text: Every crew where its order fits. The choices trade speed against isolation.

lines.speaker: Fen
lines.text: Now Feature and Docs both want to show their work at the Lookout.

lines.speaker: Fen
lines.text: Their channels are separate. So why are they stuck?

lines.speaker: Fen
lines.text: Their channels are already apart. Worktrees separate files and branches, not ports.

lines.speaker: Fen
lines.text: That's it! Different ports for parallel previews. Docs takes Lookout 5174.

lines.speaker: Fen
lines.text: That works too: stop one server. Or start the second on 5174.

lines.speaker: Fen
lines.text: Two previews on one port collide. Try again.

lines.speaker: Fen
lines.text: Worktrees separate files and branches, not everything. Dev servers, databases and ports can still collide.

lines.speaker: Fen
lines.text: Mind, the course has you work one session at a time in this chapter.

lines.speaker: Fen
lines.text: Ines wants a word about what you pack. The Signal Deck's up the stair.

lines.speaker: Fen
lines.text: Listen to those wheels turning. Music, that is.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: Fen's flumes first, Captain! He's along the boardwalk.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: Context goes in the prompt box with a few special characters. Each one's a flag.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: The at sign brings files or folders. The hash brings issues or pull requests, like number twelve.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: A slash runs a slash command. And the ampersand points to other sessions, when the prompt box offers it.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: Bring the smallest amount of useful context. Less is often more.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: First order: Copilot needs the Book App's source folder.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: Next: get a recap of your last day's work.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: Now: attach the bug report about the empty state.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: And: use what Rook's crew's session found.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: That's the one! Up she goes.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: Got a file that isn't in the repository? Drag it from your computer onto a session or agent in the sidebar.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: Not sure what commands you've got? Type a slash and read the palette. It changes with your app, plugins, skills and policy.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: Today you need two: chronicle and context. Pip will show you both.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: Rook's crew is across the Signal Bridge. Mind, it sways.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: Smallest useful context, Captain. Less is often more.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Ines first, Captain. She's on the Signal Deck, just there.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: This bough's a branch: practice empty state copy. Its empty-state message got worse on purpose.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Point to the project, select Create from, open Branches and pick our branch. New worktree, every time.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Set Mode to Plan, type hash three, pick Improve the empty state copy, and ask for a plan.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: The plan opens in the Plan tab, and Review plan takes the prompt box's place.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Back in Interactive, run the Book App and open the preview. Search hobbit, then a made-up word, and note the empty state.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Then ask it to implement the plan, check the Changes tab or pill, reload, and compare.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Pip's got the day's log up in the Chronicle Loft. Up you go.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Your turn now: a light and dark theme for the Book App, in its own worktree.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Mind how you go on that bridge, Captain.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: The chronicle can wait, Captain. Rook's crew first.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: Chronicle standup reports your work from the last day. It should list this session and its changes.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: Slash context opens the usage popup below the prompt box. So does the AI credits icon by the microphone.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: Session shows the AI credits it used. Tokens, what went to the model and back. Plan, your plan's use.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: Select the Context bar for the breakdown. Check it before you pile on more files.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: Select the session name at the top of the window for its branches, its Path and its Session ID.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: Then ask Copilot to stop the session's development server. No pull request needed.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: The Elder's waiting at the Crown, Captain. Last flight up.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: Every day goes in the ledger, Captain. Even the dull ones.

lines.speaker: Maren
lines.text: The Crown can wait, Captain. Pip's ledger first.

lines.speaker: Maren
lines.text: You've climbed above the mist, Captain. Down there, every crew works on its own bough.

lines.speaker: Maren
lines.text: Pass my Trial, and the Crown Beacon is yours to light. Nine questions.

lines.speaker: Maren
lines.text: Back for the Trial? Take your time, Captain.

lines.speaker: Maren
lines.text: The Seal of Thousand-Bough. Hold it to the Beacon, Captain.

lines.speaker: Maren
lines.text: Keelhaven's shipwrights put sessions to real work: review, debug, test and preview, then issues, pull requests and checks.

lines.speaker: Maren
lines.text: Fair winds, Captain. The Sky Basket will take you down.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: What's your fork's address, Captain? We'll paint it on the crane's sign.

lines.speaker: Ezra
lines.text: Forked it? Write its address in my register, so the harbour knows which ship is yours.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.text: Captains write to me when they can’t find a setting, and these letters have gone astray.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.text: File each one in the alcove for the area that fixes it. If one isn’t a Settings job at all, it goes back in my tray.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.text: The letters are on my desk, Captain, under the alcoves.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.text: Filed! On to the next.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.text: Right alcove, and it points you on. You manage MCP servers in the Customize view, in the sidebar.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.text: Quite right, that’s not a setting. You pick the model and effort in the model control, below the prompt box.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.text: Every letter in its place! Each alcove in my hall is an area in Settings, in the same order as the app.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.text: Select the gear at the bottom of the sidebar, and they’re listed down the left. Projects is at the foot, with each project’s own settings.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.text: A new bundle of lost letters came in, Captain. They’re on my desk, if you’d like to file them.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: I’m Suri, keeper of the mill. That gate’s your fork’s Actions tab. Pull the lever: I understand my workflows, go ahead and enable them.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: Gate’s up, so your workflows are on! Back to the crane, Captain. Come see me once your practice items are in.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: If the Repository line ever isn’t yours, you probably added the original. Add your fork from the + next to Sessions instead.

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: Setup failed! Your fork’s workflows are still off. Pull the gate lever at Suri’s mill, that’s the Actions tab, then run --yes again.

lines.speaker: Fen
lines.text: Last round! Every crew has its own channel now. Read their orders and pick where each one works.

lines.speaker: Fen
lines.text: That crew's making real changes. A new worktree keeps them apart from main, and it still runs on your machine.

lines.speaker: Fen
lines.text: That's only a quick, low-stakes look. Your current checkout's fine for that, and a new worktree's the safe default.

lines.speaker: Fen
lines.text: That crew wants the work off your deck. Cloud runs it in a cloud sandbox on GitHub's hosted infrastructure.

lines.speaker: Fen
lines.text: In the app you don't dig channels. Pick New worktree in the workspace selector, and the app makes the folder and branch.

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: Pack light! Copilot's fixing one empty-state message. What do you bring?

lines.speaker: Ines
lines.text: Last one: a letter that's on your computer, not in the repository. Get it into the session.

lines.speaker: Anders
lines.text: In the app, a question starts with + next to Sessions, then Chat. Work that needs your repository starts from the + next to your project.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: First order. Thread the blue marks with me. I want you involved the whole way, calling every turn. Which helm fits?

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: Plan would chart the whole course for your approval, then sail it straight through. You wanted to call every turn.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: Autopilot works end to end without checking in, so you wouldn’t call a single turn.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: Second order: the reef passage. The approach matters here, so we see the route before we move. Which helm?

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: Hold fast! This passage is one where the approach matters. Chart it first.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: Interactive would work it out with you, one mark at a time. Here the approach matters, so we want the whole route first.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: Approve and implement sails it in Autopilot, straight through. Leg two crosses the Shoal! Read the plan, then suggest a change.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: Exit plan mode puts us back in Interactive, and you’d prompt each step yourself. This plan only needs one fix.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: Good catch. I’ll chart her round the Shoal. Have another look.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: You could, and you’d prompt each step yourself in Interactive. But this plan’s ready now.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: It’s clear of the Shoal now. There’s nothing left to change.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: Last order. Take her home to your berth. It’s well defined, and the outcome’s clear. Which helm?

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: Interactive would check in with you at every mark. A clear, well-defined run doesn’t need that.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: Plan would chart the route for your review first. On a run this clear, there’s nothing to review.

lines.speaker: Gilda
lines.text: Ahoy, Captain! Welcome to Gilda's Model Market. Trade your starfish for a model that fits the job. Bigger models cost more.

lines.speaker: Gilda
lines.text: Pick a job from the board, then hire a model and set the effort dial.

lines.speaker: Gilda
lines.text: Auto's the house special. The app chooses a model for you, then tells you which one and why. It isn't Autopilot, mind.

lines.speaker: Gilda
lines.text: Right-sized! Here's some starfish back for hiring smart.

lines.speaker: Gilda
lines.text: That's a lot of starfish for a quick look. Auto would've done it.

lines.speaker: Gilda
lines.text: High effort for a quick look? The default would've done it.

lines.speaker: Gilda
lines.text: Not quite. This job needs more muscle. Retry with a stronger model or more effort.

lines.speaker: Gilda
lines.text: With Auto on, the effort setting's hidden. For a job this hard, turn Auto off, then pick a model and a higher effort.

lines.speaker: Gilda
lines.text: No starfish? They hide all over the islands. Come back when you've found some.

lines.speaker: Gilda
lines.text: Every job on the board, right-sized. You've got an eye for models, Captain!

lines.speaker: Gilda
lines.text: Right-sized! That's a fair price for this job.

lines.speaker: Desmond
lines.text: Welcome, Captain! This is Desmond's Model Market. Hire a model that fits the job, and pay in starfish. Bigger models cost more.

lines.speaker: Desmond
lines.text: Safe sailing, Captain! A job done here counts at every market stall.

lines.speaker: Lani
lines.text: Hello, Captain! Lani's Model Market, right here on the landing. Hire a model that fits the job. Bigger models cost more starfish.

lines.speaker: Lani
lines.text: Off up the tree? Good luck, Captain. Your starfish and your jobs go with you.
